english.notes:
(i) These regulations apply to persons driving a bus on or after 10th September 2008 or driving a lorry on or after 10th September 2009.
(ii) "Relevant vehicle" means a vehicle for which is required a driving licence of category C, C+E, D or D+E as defined in Article 3(1) of the Driving Licences Directive, or a driving licence recognised as equivalent.
(iii) "Road" means any road open to the public.
(iv) See regulation 3(2) for vehicles to which these regulations DO NOT apply.
(v) Being the holder of a certificate as required by the regulation may be evidenced by possession and production of any of the following:-
(a) a driver qualification card;
(b) a Community licence with the Community code;
(c) a driver's certificate as referred to in Article 10(3)(a) of the Directive granted to the driver by a member State; or
(d) any other document issued to the driver by a member State certifying an initial CPC or a periodic CPC .
(vi) In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, "forges" means makes a false document in order that it may be used as genuine.
(vii) See regulation 13(5), (6), (7) and (8) for details in relation to the time limits on prosecutions.
(viii) See regulation 14 for the power to seize documents.
(ix) For the offence applying to a Swiss CPC or other document, see H21546.
(x) This offence no longer applies after the 2nd December 2024 due to changes made by SI 2024/1160 to the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007. For the offence applying after this date, see H101940.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit on prosecutions:
Complex - see regulation 13 of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007.
